newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish bonds mirror gilts, mildly outperform bunds.
newsitem.headline: Irish bonds mirror gilts, mildly outperform bunds.

text.p: Irish bonds slightly outperformed German bunds in light trade on Tuesday afternoon, basking in a bond-positive backdrop as convergence trades and benign U.S. data buoyed sentiment, dealers said.
"Irish prices are being marked up. We are higher relative to bunds and probably in line with gilts in the five and 10-year area," one bond dealer said.

Riada economist Padhraig Garvey said there was very active convergence trade in Europe, especially in Spanish and Italian bonds which boosted trade. In the U.S. sentiment was buoyed by bond positive U.S. housing data released earlier.
In relative terms Garvey said Ireland was lagging behind other peripheral European markets and he expected Irish yields to narrow considerably versus bunds before the year-end.

"We are still of the opinion that the Irish market deserves to be re-rated against the likes of Italy and Spain who have seen quite pronounced convergence over the past two months so we wouldn't be surprised to see the Irish market outperform over the remaining weeks of this year," he said.
He said the Irish 10-year bond was trading 90 basis points above 10-year bunds in yield terms and was 145 over in the five year area.
"We have been narrower and we expect to be in at 75 basis points over bunds in the 10-year area and 125 basis points over or less in the five year by year-end."
By 1621 GMT the Irish five year bond due 2001 had gained 10 pence t0 101.90 to yield 5.95 percent while the 10-year bond due 2006 added 29 pence to 109.02 yielding 6.60 percent.
